event.summary: Retry promises a connection attempt but retries environment destruction
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 222bf6253bcd168db04bcbb1df20180c88306998. TLDR: after sandbox deletion fails, Hosts offers Retry with the description 'Try the connection again', but clicking it retries deleting the sandbox and its files. Details: HostRow at 5008-5020 sends only the host id and always renders that connection description. Parent on_retry at 2340-2380 reads hosts.peek(), computes deleting from current HostPhase::Deleting { failure: Some(_) }, and selects retry_environment_delete instead of retry_host. Thus both ordinary current rendering and a delayed old Retry can describe reconnecting while dispatching destruction. The patch does not bind the operation to the render. Contract: SPEC_impl.md GUI: Dioxus, 'A handler for something the user answered or confirmed acts on what the render that drew the control showed, never on state it reads when it runs.' Suggested bucket: other for established misleading action description and live operation selection. Confidence: confirmed by source; no execution performed. proposed_drop: false for the misleading UI finding. possible_cover: none for the UI mismatch. Could-be-highest: original lead considered unauthorized loss of work; available source refutes fresh destruction authority: sessions/sandbox.rs:316-341 refuses retry unless manager.sealed_failed(host), and seal destruction is already irrevocably authorized. SPEC.md:1508-1524 explicitly says 'The seal survives a restart of its Farhelm and is never lifted' and 'the helm finishes destroying any sealed sandbox it sees, whether or not it sent the Delete: after a lost reply, a failed destruction or its own restart', and says failures show 'the reason and Retry'. Original consequence preserved: an older reconnect Retry may trigger deletion, but no route to an unsealed environment is established, and the endpoint forbids it. event.summary: Retry promises a connection attempt but retries environment destruction
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 222bf6253bcd168db04bcbb1df20180c88306998; synthesis checked through tip 00de0b6c9cf206f1a7c9c5ad1c76b5b10eaf85db. TLDR: Hosts' Retry says 'Try the connection again' but can instead retry destroying a sandbox and all files/processes still in it. Captured-render contract: HostRow:5008-5020 captures only id in onclick and always draws that connection description; it carries no displayed operation discriminator. Parent on_retry:2337-2380 reads hosts.peek(), computes deleting from the current HostPhase::Deleting { failure: Some(_) }, then chooses retry_environment_delete or retry_host. The operation is therefore chosen from live state, not the render acted on. This mismatch exists even without a delayed click when the current row already reports failed deletion, and a queued reconnect Retry can change operation after its render. SPEC_impl.md GUI: Dioxus, Answers bind to what was drawn: 'A handler for something the user answered or confirmed acts on what the render that drew the control showed, never on state it reads when it runs.' Original potentially-highest interpretation PRESERVED: a control described as reconnecting can dispatch destruction and lose every remaining process/file in that environment, outside the consequence stated on that control. Endpoint checks establish a narrower authority route: sessions/sandbox.rs:316-331 first requires manager.sealed_failed(host), which manager.rs:2657-2665 defines as an existing SealedHost::Failed record; otherwise it returns Conflict and does not call finish_seal. finish_seal takes the per-host provisioning lock, then finish_seal_locked calls hosts::finish_sealed_environment, which re-reads and requires session-owned plus removal_deletes_machine before removal. SPEC.md Sandbox sessions explicitly says 'The seal survives a restart of its Farhelm and is never lifted' and 'the helm finishes destroying any sealed sandbox it sees, whether or not it sent the Delete: after a lost reply, a failed destruction or its own restart', and the initial confirmation covers every process/file. Thus source establishes retry of already irrevocably authorized destruction, with no source route from this endpoint to a fresh unsealed environment. event.detail: Reviewed commit: 350a4b33b6d4476f4a78e43cea124bc2b828f462. TLDR: the newly generalized removal-label helper tells maintainers that every machine-deleting host is labelled Delete sandbox, although Podman hosts are correctly labelled Delete container. This is a narrow documentation defect, not wrong production deletion or consent. Details: remove_label docs at hosts.rs:3718-3719 describe the item as 'Delete sandbox for a host whose removal deletes its machine, Remove for one that is only forgotten'. The changed implementation:3720-3724 now asks the host kind for its provider and returns ProviderUi(provider).host_delete_label(). That exhaustive mapping at environment_ui.rs:75-79 is Tensorlake => Delete sandbox, Podman => Delete container, while UI HostKind::removal_deletes_machine at lib.rs:987-990 returns true for both. The product and implementation contract require provider-owned wording for distinct sandboxes/containers (SPEC_impl.md Disposable environments); production meets it, and that correctness does not make the retained documentation accurate. Suggested fix: describe provider-specific whole-environment deletion labels, with ordinary hosts retaining Remove. Suggested bucket other (source documentation accuracy).
